subject.title: Gateway restart failure should keep previous instance running to avoid total disconnect

question: Should OpenClaw pursue a full old-instance-preserving gateway restart handoff, or narrow this class of failures to config fallback and doctor recovery?
rationale: Current code proves the requested behavior is not implemented, but the fix changes core restart semantics across locks, supervisors, ports, config validation, channels, and user notification paths, so automation should not choose the product boundary alone.

options.title: Design restart handoff
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical product/design track for proving replacement gateway readiness before retiring the active instance.

options.title: Narrow to config fallback
options.body: Treat invalid-config restart failures as the main product gap and route them through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/100072, leaving full atomic swap out of scope for now.

options.title: Defer semantic change
options.body: Document the current fail-closed restart behavior and rely on doctor/status recovery instead of adding a new restart handoff model.

recommendation.title: Design restart handoff
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical product/design track for proving replacement gateway readiness before retiring the active instance.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent commits in restart intent/sentinel handling and release snapshots make this the strongest current routing signal for gateway restart semantics.
